title: agent context --contract: the documented --task-only invocation is unreachable -- every --contract call reads a stdin binding and fails OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT
description:
Filed under ODOC-437 (DEC-161 context-reduction). Probable lore defect, reproduced against the released 0.12.0; NOT fixed here.

REPRODUCTION (lore-cli checkout, installed lore 0.12.0, profile .lore/agents/implementation.toml present):
  $ lore agent context implementation --task LCLI-677 --contract opum-agent-workflow/v1 --max-tokens 30000 --json
  exit 1; stdout BYTE-EMPTY; stderr: OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT
Controls, same tree:
  - without --contract (same budget): exit 0, kind agent.context.export.
  - with --contract AND a valid binding on stdin (contract opum-agent-workflow, supportedVersions [1], requestId 32-hex, taskId LCLI-677, profileId implementation): exit 0, a full opum-agent-workflow record (profileRevision, digest, contextId, sourceIds). So the contract feature is NOT broken -- it works when called with a binding.
  - the failure does not depend on the budget: it reproduces at --max-tokens 2000 and 30000.

CAUSE (src/commands/agent.ts): runContextContract (lines 344-350) routes EVERY --contract invocation to runWorkflowBinding, whether or not --task is present. runWorkflowBinding (lines 226-239) reads the request binding from stdin when neither --request nor --request-file is given (lines 229-232); an empty stdin makes raw.trim() the empty string and throws WorkflowBindingError(OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT, binding is empty) at lines 233-234. emitBindingFailure (lines 321-336) then writes only the marker to stderr, leaves stdout byte-empty, and exits 1 -- by the strict contract. So the marker does NOT mean lore is absent: it means the request binding is empty or absent.

VERDICT: a DEFECT, not merely a missing-configuration message -- a documentation/implementation divergence on a documented surface:
  - docs/reference/cli-surface.md:949 and src/core/manifest.ts:938 publish the example `lore agent context <profile> --task <taskId> --contract opum-agent-workflow/v1 --json`, the exact shape that fails. It is user-visible: `lore help agent` prints it (the manifest drives that help).
  - docs/reference/cli-surface.md:958 states that the --task-only form serves the read-only projection, while line 959 documents the stdin-binding form for the NO---task case. The docs describe two mechanisms; the implementation has only the second.
  - src/commands/agent.ts:337-341 still carries a docstring advertising that facade (Facade: lore agent context <profile> --task <taskId> --contract ...), contradicting the docstring at 217-224 (with no --task) and the comment at 344-348 (owns EVERY --contract invocation).
  - Secondary: the marker OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT is overloaded and misdirects. Two measured triggers for the same marker: an empty or absent binding (line 234), and a not_found from profile or task resolution (lines 326-327), so a valid binding naming a missing profile also exits 1 with OPUM_WORKFLOW_LORE_ABSENT. cli-contract.md:504 documents only the second. A caller reading LORE_ABSENT looks for a missing lore install, not for a missing stdin binding.

NOT DECIDED HERE (design question for opum-doc): should the documented --task-only form serve the projection (docs right, the delegation is a regression), or must a binding always be supplied (code right, in which case the two cli-surface examples, the manifest example and the 337-341 docstring are stale)? Either way, the two meanings of the marker should be separated or documented.

CITED: ODOC-437 (opum-doc, DEC-161 context-reduction work). Reproduced by lore-cli at the leader request; the opum-cli session measured the same shape on installed 0.12.0 in its own repository.
